# R0 — Series + Author Prefaces (lines 131–166)

**Range read in full:** 131–166  
**Source:** Osborne, *Revelation* (BECNT, 2002)

## Claims

### C1 — BECNT series aim (Silva)
**Locus:** 131–151  
**Quote:** "The chief concern of the Baker Exegetical Commentary on the New Testament … is to provide, within the framework of informed evangelical thought, commentaries that blend scholarly depth with readability…"  
**Claim:** Series targets pastors and serious lay readers; focuses problems that bear on text meaning; stresses paragraph-level argument development; engages critical scholarship without assimilation or dismissive interaction; assumes trustworthiness and essential unity of Scripture and historic creeds as legitimate framework.

### C2 — Author’s purpose: theological threads + intertextuality
**Locus:** 153–157  
**Quote:** "The purpose of this commentary is not only to provide the reader with exegetical and background information on the text but to help the reader trace the theological threads that tie the book together."  
**Claim:** Osborne prioritizes intertextual data and key-word overviews across the Apocalypse with theological commentary on each theme. "Apocalypse" and "Revelation" used interchangeably.

### C3 — Resource for scholarly divides
**Locus:** 157–159  
**Quote:** "I want to make this a resource so that students can know where scholarship divides on key issues. Thus I often have fairly lengthy lists of scholars with the various options on an exegetical debate."  
**Claim:** Lengthy option-lists omit author-date when multiple names share a view (except articles or single holders) to avoid clutter; standard author-date used otherwise.

### C4 — Institutional provenance
**Locus:** 161–163  
**Claim:** TEDS sabbatical; Baker editors Wells Turner and Moisés Silva; research TAs named (Sung-Min Park, Ben Kim, Dana Harris, Love Sechrest, Christine Poston, Bill Myatt). Dedication (front matter earlier): mentors Wes Gerig, Richard Longenecker, Clark Pinnock, I. Howard Marshall.

## Coverage
Read lines 131–166 complete. No body commentary in this range.
